examples.name: First Look
examples.description: prompt bound to a schema with -> Review, plus offline validate
examples.learningGoal: See how -> Review binds a prompt to a schema before the syntax tutorial.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a rendered review prompt and a schema-ok line.

examples.name: Hello World
examples.learningGoal: Run a one-line MALDA program and change visible output.

examples.name: Input Example
examples.description: Using input() to read user input
examples.learningGoal: Capture user input, convert text to numbers, and respond with computed output.
examples.expectedOutput: Prompts for a name and age, then prints a personalized message.

examples.name: Variables and Arithmetic
examples.learningGoal: Store values in variables and combine them with arithmetic expressions.

examples.name: Conditionals
examples.learningGoal: Choose different code paths based on a condition.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints different messages depending on variable values.

examples.name: While Loop
examples.learningGoal: Repeat work while a condition stays true.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a sequence generated by a loop.

examples.name: For Loop
examples.learningGoal: Use MALDA's for loop to repeat a block with a clear loop variable.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints values generated by a for loop.

examples.name: Functions
examples.learningGoal: Organize repeated logic into reusable functions.
examples.expectedOutput: Calls a function and prints its result.

examples.name: Errors and Match
examples.description: try/catch/finally, tagged catch with kind, and match expressions
examples.learningGoal: Handle failures and branch on values with match before moving to richer programs.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints caught errors, cleanup from finally, and match labels for a status code.

examples.name: Schema Validate
examples.description: schema declaration plus validate() returning { ok, data|error }
examples.learningGoal: Validate structured values without relying on type hints or thrown parseJson errors.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints an ok Person line and an expected age-type failure.

examples.name: Modules with Include
examples.description: Split helpers into another file and splice them with include
examples.learningGoal: Reuse functions across files with include (splice), distinct from import/export packages.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a greeting and a small addition from an included helper file.

examples.name: Complete Starter Program
examples.description: A small end-to-end example that combines variables, arrays, loops, functions, and conditionals
examples.learningGoal: See how the basic MALDA syntax fits together in one small real program.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints the number of items, the total cost, and a small summary label.

examples.name: Dictionary Example
examples.description: Create a dictionary, read and write entries, and inspect keys and values
examples.learningGoal: Learn how MALDA stores and updates key-value data.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints dictionary values, key presence checks, and collection lengths.

examples.name: Async All Example
examples.description: Run multiple async computations and await them together with all()
examples.learningGoal: Understand MALDA's basic structured concurrency workflow.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints 3 after both async computations complete.

examples.name: Lambdas and Arrays
examples.description: Comprehensive examples of lambda expressions and array methods
examples.learningGoal: Move from basic functions into more expressive array and lambda patterns.
examples.expectedOutput: Shows array operations powered by lambda expressions.
